newsitem.title: NORWAY: Gasline plans submitted for Norne, Heidrun fields.
newsitem.headline: Gasline plans submitted for Norne, Heidrun fields.

text.p: Den norske stats oljeselskap AS (Statoil) said on Thursday plans had been submitted to the Oil Ministry for the installation and operation of gas pipelines from the Heidrun and Norne fields in the Haltenbanken off mid-Norway.
Statoil's Status Weekly newsletter said the plans were based on a call by Norway's Gas Supply Committee (FU) to secure a gas delivery solution for the two fields.
The licensees of the developments have applied to export one billion cubic metres of gas per year from each field from 2000.

Statoil said that if the FU's proposals were approved, pipelines running 121 km and 37 km from Norne and Heidrun respectively would eventually be tied into the export riser base for the Aasgard trunkline.
From there, the gas would flow to the Kaarstoe terminal, north of Stavanger on the west coast of Norway, and on to continental Europe.
Statoil put investment at 650 million crowns for the Norne line and 720 million crowns for Heidrun.
